title: akashi.audit-report/1
description: One answer, audited against the ContextPackage that produced it. A report says which load-bearing strings of the answer are in the text that was sent, and where. It says nothing about whether the answer is true.

contract.description: Read first. A consumer that does not recognise the value refuses the report rather than guessing at it. `1-draft` is emitted until a second program has produced and consumed one; the freeze is a condition, not a date.

report_id.description: sha256 over exactly what determined the report: the response, the package, the akashi version, the segmenters, the extractors and the language packs. Not the clock, and not the findings -- a report whose id covered its own findings could not be used to check that they were re-derived correctly.

package_id.description: The ContextPackage this was audited against. Empty when the producer set none.

segmenters.description: Every count on this report has these in its denominator (ADR-0009), so a recheck that produced different numbers can attribute the difference.

packs.description: The language packs that were loaded. Narrowing them changes the segmentation and therefore every count, which is why they are in the report_id.

matcher.description: Which strings counted as the same string. akashi ships 'normalized' -- folded form, a particular's internal spacing free, and a match rejected when it sits inside a longer token of the same kind -- and 'exact', which is the same boundary rules with no spacing tolerance. This is in report_id for the same reason the language packs are: it changes every count on the report, and two runs that answered it differently must not be able to claim one id. Required: a report that does not say which one produced it cannot be re-derived.

unchecked.description: Every span akashi did not examine, each with the rule that caused it. Required, and empty only when nothing was skipped: a partial check reported as a single number reads as a total check (ADR-0005).

coverage.description: The denominators, published so a reader cannot assume the wrong one -- and they assume the generous one.

bearing.description: Examined, and holding at least one particular.

unbearing.description: Examined, and holding nothing to check. Not a pass.

unexamined.description: Not examined at all. Different from unbearing, and kept apart because a check that treats 'I looked and found nothing wrong' the same as 'I did not look' lies by omission.

kinds_not_extracted.description: Kinds in the vocabulary that no loaded rule finds. A blind spot that is not named reads as an absence of findings.

limits.description: What the method cannot do, on the artefact rather than in the documentation. The artefact travels and the documentation does not. Fixed wording: a caller who could reword it could soften it.

segments.description: Every verdict, including the ones that are zero. A verdict missing from a summary reads as a verdict that cannot happen.

grounded_share.description: Grounded particulars over checked ones. **null when nothing was checkable** -- not 0 and not 1. An answer with nothing to check has not scored well and has not scored badly, and a number here would be read as one of the two.

restoration_asserted.description: True when restored_by is the caller's word rather than something akashi watched happen (ADR-0013). A renderer must keep the two apart in wording as well as in data.

withheld.description: How many candidates the package held back, per rule. Context for the reader and never an explanation of any finding: an omission carries no text, so akashi cannot check an answer against it (ADR-0012).

unrecognised.description: Dotted paths to fields the ContextPackage carried that its own contract does not list. tsumugi.context-package/1 is closed and every object in it sets additionalProperties: false, so a package carrying one of these does not conform to the contract it names -- and akashi audited it anyway. Context about the document, on the same footing as withheld: never an explanation of any finding (ADR-0012). Empty for a conforming package.

judged.description: What a language model said about the claims akashi could not settle, each under the name of the model that said it. NOT verdicts and NOT in report_id: akashi's verdicts are decided by comparing strings and are the same on every machine on every day; these are not. A consumer must keep the two apart -- 'supported' means a model thought the evidence entails the claim, while 'grounded' means the string is in the text that was sent. Empty unless a judge ran (ADR-0017).

model.description: Who answered. Required: two runs against two model versions are two different answers, and a reader who cannot tell them apart cannot act on either.

answer.description: The text that was audited, verbatim. A report is complete on its own: every span in it indexes this string, so a reader needs nothing else to follow a finding.

span.description: A half-open range of code-point offsets into `answer`, or into a source document where the object says so.

verdict.description: Three of these mean akashi found nothing wrong, for three different reasons. `contradicted` is defined and produced by nothing before v0.4.

layer.description: kiseki's distinction, and it survives the crossing. A particular grounded in an interpretation is grounded in an interpretation.

reason.description: Why this span met the rule. Required and non-empty: a skip with no reason is a silent gap.

location.description: One place a particular was found, in document coordinates. Not item coordinates: a reader opens the file, and the file does not know it was cut into items.

locations.description: Every place it stands alone in the text that was sent. Present only when it grounded, and more than one is information rather than an error.

in_an_interpretation.description: Grounded, and every place it was found was already a judgement.

script.description: For reporting only. Nothing in segmentation depends on it (ADR-0011).

boundary.description: Why the segment ended where it did. `line` is the weaker fallback rule, and a report can say how much of an answer it cut.

because.description: Why akashi did not examine this segment. Present exactly when the verdict is `unchecked` or `unverifiable`.

contradiction.description: What the text that was sent says, where this particular says something else. Present only on a particular that is still floating -- it resolved nowhere, which is why it is a finding at all. akashi emits this only where the answer kept the source's digits exactly and changed the text around them; a value whose digits differ from every source value is left floating without one.

found.description: The source's text, verbatim. Not a correction: akashi does not know which of the two is right, only that they differ.

why.description: The rule that produced this finding, in words. A finding that cannot say why it is a finding is one nobody can appeal.
